Test standardized measures against a reference value

Source: R/test_measure.R
test_measure.Rd

Measure-level z test. With a transformation \(g\) (identity, logit or log) the statistic is $$z_i = \frac{g(M_i) - g(M_{ref})}{g'(M_i)\, SE_i}.$$ Under the null, \(z_i\) follows \(N(\mathrm{location}, \mathrm{scale}^2)\): location = 0, scale = 1 is the theoretical null, a fixed inflation such as scale = 1.81 is a known-scale null, and the location and scale of an empirical null can be passed per provider.

Usage

test_measure(
  estimate,
  se,
  reference,
  transform = c("identity", "logit", "log"),
  location = 0,
  scale = 1,
  level = 0.95,
  critical = NULL,
  ci_location = location,
  alternative = c("two.sided", "greater", "less"),
  providers = NULL,
  null_model = NULL
)

Arguments

estimate

the standardized measures \(M_i\), one per provider.

se

their standard errors.

reference

the reference value \(M_{ref}\) (one number or one value per provider), for instance the population rate.

transform

"identity" (default), "logit" or "log".

location, scale

location and scale of the null distribution of \(z\) (one number or one value per provider).

level

confidence level. Default 0.95.

critical

critical value; defaults to the normal quantile for level.

ci_location

location used to centre the confidence interval; defaults to location.

alternative

"two.sided" (default), "greater" or "less".

providers

optional provider identifiers for the output.

null_model

optional null model (a pp_null object or a function of the result returning one), applied through calibrate(); it replaces location and scale.

Value

A data frame of class pp_measure_test with one row per provider: provider (if given), estimate, se, reference, estimate_t, se_t, reference_t (on the transformed scale), z, p, flag (1 above the reference, -1 below, 0 not different, NA when z is missing), lower, upper (measure scale) and lower_t, upper_t.

Details

The interval inverts the calibrated test: \(g(M_i) - (\mathrm{ci\_location} \pm \mathrm{critical} \cdot \mathrm{scale})\, SE_i^{(g)}\), mapped back with \(g^{-1}\). One-sided alternatives give one-sided intervals.

Examples

test_measure(estimate = c(0.12, 0.30, 0.22), se = c(0.03, 0.04, 0.05),
             reference = 0.2, transform = "logit")
#>   estimate   se reference estimate_t      se_t reference_t          z
#> 1     0.12 0.03       0.2 -1.9924302 0.2840909   -1.386294 -2.1335980
#> 2     0.30 0.04       0.2 -0.8472979 0.1904762   -1.386294  2.8297316
#> 3     0.22 0.05       0.2 -1.2656664 0.2913753   -1.386294  0.4139953
#>             p flag      lower     upper   lower_t    upper_t
#> 1 0.032875700   -1 0.07247769 0.1922242 -2.549238 -1.4356222
#> 2 0.004658706    1 0.22782660 0.3836767 -1.220624 -0.4739714
#> 3 0.678877583    0 0.13743595 0.3330147 -1.836751 -0.6945813
